Adapting models to concept drift

Source: vignettes/adaptive-models.Rmd
adaptive-models.Rmd

Detecting a drift is only useful if the model reacts to it. stealthy() wraps a classifier and a drift detector: at every call to fit() it checks the new batch for drift and, when one is found, discards the old training data and retrains the model on the new concept.

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)

A stream with real concept drift

The stream below has two numeric features drawn from the same distribution during the whole stream. Only the rule that defines the target changes: up to observation 750 the target is x1 + x2 > 0, and from then on it is x1 - x2 > 0. This is real concept drift, because the inputs look the same but their relationship with the target has changed.

set.seed(1)
n <- 1500
x <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n))
new_concept <- seq_len(n) > 750
target <- ifelse(new_concept, x$x1 - x$x2 > 0, x$x1 + x$x2 > 0)
y <- data.frame(target = factor(target, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)))

batch <- (seq_len(n) - 1) %/% 50 + 1

Training and testing batch by batch

The stream is processed in batches of 50 observations. Each batch is first used to test the current model and is then given to fit(), which updates the model with it. The classifier is a naive Bayes model from daltoolbox.

run_stream <- function(detector) {
  model <- stealthy(cla_nb("target", c("FALSE", "TRUE")), detector, warmup_size = 100)
  results <- NULL
  for (b in 2:max(batch)) {
    train <- batch == (b - 1)
    test <- batch == b
    model <- fit(model, x[train, ], y[train, , drop = FALSE])

    accuracy <- NA
    if (model$fitted) {
      prediction <- predict(model, x[test, ])
      accuracy <- mean((prediction[, 2] > 0.5) == (y$target[test] == "TRUE"))
    }
    results <- rbind(results, data.frame(batch = b, drifted = model$drifted, accuracy = accuracy))
  }
  results
}

dfr_inactive() never reports a drift, so that model keeps accumulating data from both concepts. dfr_ddm() monitors the mistakes of the classifier.

without_detector <- run_stream(dfr_inactive())
with_ddm <- run_stream(dfr_ddm())

with_ddm[with_ddm$drifted, ]
#>    batch drifted accuracy
#> 9     10    TRUE       NA
#> 17    18    TRUE       NA
#> 20    21    TRUE       NA
#> 23    24    TRUE       NA
#> 25    26    TRUE       NA

After the drift is detected, the model needs warmup_size observations before it is trained again, which is why the accuracy is missing for one batch.

plot(without_detector$batch, without_detector$accuracy,
  type = "b", pch = 16,
  ylim = c(0.4, 1), col = "grey50", xlab = "batch", ylab = "accuracy"
)
lines(with_ddm$batch, with_ddm$accuracy, type = "b", pch = 16, col = "steelblue")
abline(v = 750 / 50 + 0.5, lty = 2, col = "grey70")
legend("bottomleft", c("dfr_inactive()", "dfr_ddm()"),
  col = c("grey50", "steelblue"),
  pch = 16, bty = "n", cex = 0.8
)

after <- with_ddm$batch > 16
c(
  without_detector = mean(without_detector$accuracy[after], na.rm = TRUE),
  with_ddm = mean(with_ddm$accuracy[after], na.rm = TRUE)
)
#> without_detector         with_ddm 
#>        0.4457143        0.9100000

Choosing the detector

stealthy() decides what to feed the detector from its class:

  • error-based detectors (such as dfr_ddm()) receive the mistakes of the model on the new batch, so they react to real concept drift;
  • distribution-based detectors with a target_feat (such as dfr_kswin(target_feat = "x1")) receive that feature, and without one they receive the row means of the normalized features, so they react to virtual concept drift;
  • multivariate detectors (dfr_aedd()) and dfr_multi_criteria() receive all the normalized features.

In the stream above the inputs never change, so only an error-based detector can notice the drift. When labels arrive late or not at all, a distribution-based detector is the only option, at the cost of missing changes that do not affect the inputs.

Factor, character and logical features are one-hot encoded automatically, and levels that appear only after training are encoded as zeros.
